---
title: "Pipeline"
---

Scripts are numbered in the order they run. Each one writes to
`<DATA_ROOT>/data/outputs/` and reads what the previous step wrote. Run them from the
repository root:

```bash
uv run python scripts/20_subsets/21_prepare_input_data.py
```

Most steps take minutes. The two model scripts are the slow ones, but not by as much
as the numbers in older notes suggest: `31_shap.py` takes about 20 minutes for all 208
sites on a 24-thread machine.

## Run variants

Every stage from 21 onwards carries a `VARIANT` constant at the top of the script:

```python
VARIANT = ""          # the paths behind the submitted results
VARIANT = "deep-sm"   # a sensitivity run, in its own folder
```

An empty string reads and writes the baseline paths. Any other value inserts a folder
level on both sides, so a variant reads `20_subsets/<VARIANT>/` and writes
`30_shap/<FLUX>/<type>/<VARIANT>/`. Input and output move together on purpose: a run
that read baseline subsets and wrote variant results would finish without an error and
produce numbers that mean nothing.

Scripts 41 to 44 and the figure scripts take a second switch alongside it:

```python
SITE_SUBSET = ""              # every site
SITE_SUBSET = "deeper-only"   # the 128 sites whose soil water is below layer 1
```

It adds another folder level, so the four combinations land in four places and none of
them overwrites another:

| VARIANT | SITE_SUBSET | what it holds |
|---|---|---|
| empty | empty | the submitted analysis, 208 sites, shallow soil water |
| `deep-sm` | empty | 128 sites deep and 80 shallow, since sites without a usable deeper layer stay on layer 1 |
| empty | `deeper-only` | the shallow arm of the matched comparison, 128 sites |
| `deep-sm` | `deeper-only` | the deep arm, the same 128 sites |

The last two are the pair that isolates depth. Same sites, same records, only the sensor
differs. See [Methods](methods.qmd#soil-water-depth).

Set the same value in every stage of a variant run. A stage whose predecessor has not
run with that variant fails on a missing file rather than falling back to the baseline.

`31_shap.py` and `32_validate_shap_methods.py` also take `SITES` and `MAX_SITES`, which
limit a run to a few sites for timing. `SITES` names them and wins if it is not empty,
`MAX_SITES` takes the first n rows, and 0 means all sites. Both scripts report how long
each site took and what that implies for the full list.

## 10_datasets: assemble the site collection

| Script | What it does | Writes |
|--------|--------------|--------|
| `00_find_overlaps.py` | Lists sites present in both AmeriFlux and FLUXNET-SHUTTLE. **Deletes source folders, see the warning below** | `10_datasets/` |
| `11_collect_info.py` | Scans all five raw sources, one row per dataset found | `11_datasets_info.csv` |
| `12_create_parquet.py` | Merges the datasets of a site into one parquet file, resolving frequency and overlapping years by source priority | `12_parquet_merged/`, `12_datasets_info_parquet.csv` |
| `13_check_available_vars.py` | Records which of NEE, LE, GPP, RECO, TA, VPD, SWIN, SWC exist per site and under which column name | `13_datasets_info_parquet_vars.csv` |
| `13b_check_available_vars_SWC.py` | Same for the soil moisture depth variants, plus one row per site and variable with peak-month coverage and a ratio against layer 1 | `13b_variables_coverage_summary.csv`, `13b_variables_per_site.csv` |
| `14_collect_basic_stats.py` | Record counts, date ranges, min/max/mean per variable | `14_datasets_info_parquet_vars_stats.csv` |
| `15_remove_sites.py` | Applies the inclusion criteria and drops the rest | `15_datasets_info_parquet_vars_stats_usedsites.csv` |
| `16a` + `16b` | ERA5 1991-2020 normals from Google Earth Engine, run in parallel batches | `16_ERA5_climate_1991-2020_GoogleEarthEngine/` |
| `16c` + `16d` | Same from the Copernicus CDS API | `16_ERA5_climate_1991-2020_Copernicus/` |
| `16_download_era5_mat_map.py` | CDS download for the older FLUXNET2015 sites, which carry no 1991-2020 ERA5 in their own files | `16_ERA5_climate_1991-2020/` |
| `17_add_era5_info.py` | Picks one ERA5 source per site and adds MAT and MAP | `17_datasets_info_parquet_vars_stats_usedsites_era5.csv` |

::: {.callout-warning title="00_find_overlaps.py deletes data"}
`DELETE_OVERLAPPING_FOLDERS = True` is the committed default, and the script removes
AmeriFlux source folders for sites that also exist in FLUXNET-SHUTTLE. The site
collection in `11_collect_info.py` onwards already reflects that decision, so there is
no reason to run it again.
:::

The `16*` scripts need credentials and can be skipped if the ERA5 output folders are
already populated. Script `17` writes a timestamped log with the full decision trail
for every site.

## 20_subsets: build the model input

`21_prepare_input_data.py` turns each merged site parquet into the subset the models
see. Per site:

1. keep the four months with the highest mean GPP
2. keep measured NEE only, quality flag 0, no gap-filled fluxes
3. keep daytime records, `SW_IN_POT > 20`
4. balance the record so every one of the four months contributes the same number of
   years, dropping the oldest years where needed
5. drop records with any missing predictor
6. derive ET from LE and TA, and NEP as `-NEE`
7. z-score every variable within the site and keep both the measured and the z-scored
   columns

`22_data_flow.py` counts how many records each filtering step removes, per site, and
writes `22_data_flow.csv`. It walks the same filters in the same order as `21` and then
checks its final count against `N_RECORDS` from `21` for every site, refusing to write
the table on any mismatch. Over the 209 sites that enter stage 21, 7.1 % of delivered
half-hourly records reach the models, and the largest single loss is the QC filter, 26.8
million records, because the analysis uses measured NEE only.

Writes one parquet per site to `20_subsets/<VARIANT>/21_subsets_parquet/`, a heatmap
per site, and the summary table `21_SUBSETS_parquet_vars_stats_subsets.csv`. The
summary records `SWC_VAR` and `SWC_LAYER`, so a later comparison can tell which soil
water layer went into which site.

Sites run in parallel, `N_WORKERS = 3` by default. Memory sets that limit, not cores:
the largest sites need about 3 GB per worker. With `N_WORKERS = 1` the sites run one
after the other and the plots are shown on screen.

The soil water layer is chosen here:

```python
SWC_LAYER = "shallow"   # SWC_F_MDS_1, as in the submitted analysis
SWC_LAYER = "deepest"   # deepest usable layer per site
```

See [Methods](methods.qmd#soil-water-depth) for the selection rule and what the deep
run showed.

::: {.callout-note}
One site, CD-Ygb, has VPD in the wrong units in the source files. The correction is
applied in this script.
:::

## 30_shap: fit models and explain them

`31_shap.py` trains the models and calculates SHAP values. It has two modes, switched
at the top of the file:

```python
TUNE_HYPERPARAMETERS = False   # SHAP analysis (default)
TUNE_HYPERPARAMETERS = True    # hyperparameter search instead
TUNE_N_ITER = 25               # combinations tested per site in tuning mode
```

`CV_STRATEGY` picks the cross-validation scheme, `random` for the shuffled 5-fold split
behind the published results or `blocked` for leave-one-year-out. See
[Methods](methods.qmd) for what changes between them.

In SHAP mode each site gets 5-fold cross-validation. Within each fold the 80 % training
part is split again into 68 % for fitting and 12 % for early stopping, and the held-out
20 % is explained. Every observation therefore receives SHAP values from a model that
never saw it. Per-fold R² and RMSE go to the log, and the folds are reassembled in the
original index order.

Writes per-site parquet and CSV with features, SHAP values and predictions, plus one
aggregated CSV holding the fold metrics for all sites.

Sites left on the same input produce bit-identical output between runs, which makes a
useful check when only some sites change: rerun with a variant, and every unchanged
site should come back identical.

`32_validate_shap_methods.py` fits one model per site on an 85/15 split and calculates
ALE curves on 100 grid points per feature. ALE is a second read on the same fitted
models: it shows the isolated effect of a feature on the prediction, where SHAP
attributes each individual prediction. Writes `{SITE}_ale_curves_{TARGET}.csv` per site,
which is what the aggregation and figure scripts consume.

## 40_aggregation: combine site results

| Script | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `41_binagg_per_site.py` | Bins each site's SHAP values on a two-variable grid, using fixed custom bin edges so all sites share one grid |
| `42_binagg_across_sites.py` | Averages the binned grids across all sites, one vote per site |
| `43_binagg_across_igbp.py` | Same, separately per IGBP forest type |
| `44_agg_per_scenario.py` | Averages SHAP values within the nine stress stages, per site and then across sites |

Equal weighting throughout: a site with 20 years of data counts the same as a site with
three. Bins that fewer than half of the sites reach are dropped from the aggregated
grids.

Scripts 41 to 43 loop over `VAR_PAIRS`, the five x/y combinations the figures need:

| x | y |
|---|---|
| TA | VPD |
| SWC | VPD |
| TA | SWC |
| ET | VPD |
| ET | SWC |

One run of each script covers all five. Script 44 takes no pair and runs once.

Order matters: 41 first, then 42 and 43, which read what 41 wrote. Those two can run at
the same time as each other, since they write different files. Script 44 reads the SHAP
output directly and can run at any point after 31. Timings on 208 sites: 41 takes about
40 minutes because it reads every site file once per pair, 42 is a minute, 43 about ten,
44 a minute.

## 50_figures

Each figure script reads the aggregation output and writes to
`50_plots/<FLUX>/<type>/<VARIANT>/`, so a variant cannot overwrite a published figure.

Script 51 (the site map) has no variant and needs none, since the site list does not
depend on which soil water layer was used. Script 55 reads the ALE output, so script 32
has to have run with the same variant first.

Three scripts here produce tables rather than manuscript figures:

| Script | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `57_fig_data_flow_sankey.py` | Draws `22_data_flow.csv` as a Sankey, one ribbon narrowing at each filtering step |
| `58_threshold_zscore_to_kpa.py` | Converts the threshold from sigma to kPa per site, then averages, and reproduces the published values |
| `59_biome_threshold_significance.py` | One threshold per site, then Kruskal-Wallis and Holm-corrected pairwise tests between forest types |

Script 52 draws both Figure 2 and Extended Data Figure 2 and picks between them by which
of two blocks near the top is commented out. Running it twice, once per block, gives
both.

See [Figures](figures.qmd) for what each one shows.
